messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat_low_rate for customer 'acme-med' — severity: P1 — PagerDuty incident: PD-82451
pagerduty: Incident PD-82451 created and sent to primary on-call.
sasha: ackd — looking now, grabbing logs from the controlplane host in us-west-2.
mike: on it too, will check agent heartbeats and sg/routing.
jen: pinging the customer's networking contact to confirm anything on their FTW side. 
ian: customer reports intermittent internal API 502s earlier, might be related. ticket #ACME-1123 opened.
sasha: quick checks — controlplane k8s nodes show controlplane-agent pod RestartCount=2 on cp-3. KV cache staleness increasing in metrics.
mike: netstat shows lots of TIME_WAIT but controlplane <-> agent TLS handshakes failing with TLS alert 40. suspect MTU or pf rules.
jen: customer says they rolled out an iptables change around 09:12 local earlier. asking if they can revert or test.
sasha: runbook step 1: try agent soft-restart on affected host: `systemctl restart redwood-agent` then `journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager`.
mike: running soft-restart on cp-3 now. tail shows `ERR peer handshake: i/o timeout` still.
ian: customer: reverting iptables now, will update in 30s.
jen: they reverted, waiting on their side.
sasha: metrics: heartbeat rate jumped back up ~20s after revert — partial recovery. latency to controlplane API still high for ~5% of requests.
mike: did a controlplane-agent full restart and bumped loglevel to debug, capturing handshake traces: `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.3.5:8443 -msg -brief` shows retransmits.
incident-bot: PD-82451 acknowledged by sasha at 2026-03-15T12:34:10Z.
pagerduty: Notified escalation targets: network-eng, oncall-night.
sasha: tagging @lee-oncall-next for handoff — I need to step out in 15m. I'll leave mitigation steps and what to watch.
lee-oncall-next: thanks, I'll take the remainder. pls leave the `tcpdump` capture on cp-3 for 30m and share path.
sasha: /var/log/redwood/diag/pd-82451-cp3.tgz uploading to s3://redwood-incident-logs/PD-82451/cp3.tgz — link: https://s3.redwood.company/PD-82451/cp3.tgz
mike: workaround applied: added temporary route via mgmt-proxy to bypass customer transit for controlplane traffic. expected to reduce TLS failures.
ian: customer confirms controlplane API errors dropped to <1% after route change. They still see occasional 504s for long-running calls.
jen: raising a post-incident action: verify iptables change window and add guardrail in onboarding doc for customers.
sasha: handoff notes for @lee-oncall-next: watch heartbeat_rate, controlplane_errors_5m, and agent_restart_count. If errors >5% for 10m, escalate to network-eng + customer-ops. Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.company/runbooks/private-controlplane-heartbeat
lee-oncall-next: ack. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate with customer ops. will escalate if it regresses. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident PD-82451 status changed to "under investigation".
pagerduty: Scheduled follow-up: on-call review in 30m; assign postmortem owner.
ian: I'll coordinate the customer update and set expectation window for RCA.
jen: adding note: check for any other customers that had iptables changes in same time window — running query now.
mike: capturing a few more debug traces then will revert the temporary route if stable for 15m.
sasha: thanks team — leaving the channel. handing over to lee.
lee-oncall-next: confirmed stable at 12:47Z. I'll keep PD incident open until we validate full recovery and customer signoff. planning to schedule a short sync with network-eng at +1h.
incident-bot: PD-82451 remains open. Final log bundle path: s3://redwood-incident-logs/PD-82451/all-archives.tgz
note: This thread contains automated pager notifications, acknowledgements, live mitigation steps, customer coordination, and on-call handoff for a private/VPC control plane heartbeat degradation impacting an on-prem customer agent.
